CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in bilateral hands

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
60-year-old right-handed male referred for evaluation of numbness and tingling in bilateral hands for several weeks. Patient reports motor vehicle accident in December with bilateral wrist fractures. After healing, he noticed increased tingling and numbness, which has worsened significantly over the last month. On the right side, symptoms extend from the middle and ring fingers up the forearm. On the left side, symptoms extend from the pinky and ring finger. Patient describes symptoms as mainly soreness with occasional throbbing and associated weakness, particularly with hand use. Tingling is more prominent when pain is present and becomes duller when pain resolves. Symptoms occur primarily at night and come and go throughout the day. Denies loss of sensation but reports decreased sensitivity. Patient was prescribed nerve pain medication but reports poor compliance. Also reports mild neck stiffness since hitting his head during the accident, noted to be a contusion at that time.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: Fatigue and weight gain noted
Eyes: Floaters present
Cardiovascular: Shortness of breath and leg swelling
Gastrointestinal: Excessive appetite and bloating
Endocrine: Constant hunger
Skin: Nail bed changes, dryness, and itching
Musculoskeletal: History of gout and muscle pain
Remainder of review of systems: Negative

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Motor vehicle accident in December with bilateral wrist fractures (now healed)
Head contusion from same accident
Prediabetes (controlled with diet modification)
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Coreg (for hypertension)
Lexapro (for anxiety)
Nerve pain medication (prescribed but not taking as directed)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is right-handed. Currently wearing bilateral wrist splints, particularly the right which provides symptomatic relief.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurologic examination:
- Sensation: Normal overall; diminished pin prick sensation in third and fourth fingers on right hand; decreased sensation in fourth and fifth fingers on left hand
- Reflexes: 1+ and symmetric in upper extremities; 2+ in knees; toes downgoing bilaterally
- Tinel sign: Positive at both wrists and both elbows, with patient reporting sharp sensation radiating up wrist into elbow bilaterally
- Remainder of exam: Normal

RESULTS
Clinical presentation and examination findings suggest bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, possibly with bilateral cubital tunnel involvement. Nerve irritation likely related to past wrist trauma.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome vs. bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome
Plan:
1. Schedule electromyography (EMG) test to precisely localize nerve irritation
2. Continue bilateral wrist splints
3. Follow-up visit after EMG testing
4. If symptoms persist after testing, consider referral to hand clinic for possible injections or carpal tunnel release surgery, or referral to orthopedics for similar treatment options
5. Encourage compliance with prescribed nerve pain medication
